config_name: ROG Flow Z13 — Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, Radeon 8060S (integrated), 64GB LPDDR5 unified, 1TB SSD, 13.4" 2.5K 180Hz touch

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo, 16-core Zen 5, up to 5.1 GHz)
specs.ram_type: LPDDR5-8000 soldered unified (up to 48 GB allocatable as VRAM)
specs.display_type: IPS touchscreen, 16:10, no PWM, no HDR
specs.ports: 2x USB4 40Gbps (DP 2.1, PD 3.0), 1x USB-A 3.2 Gen2, HDMI 2.1, microSD, 3.5mm, ROG XG Mobile port
specs.keyboard_notes: Detachable magnetic keyboard cover (leather-like, doubles as screen protector); ~1.23 kg tablet alone, 1.62 kg with cover

battery.notes: 70Wh. NBC measured the 32GB SKU: WiFi websurfing 9h20, video 12h44, load 0h51. NBC notes 64/128GB SKUs have higher peak power draw; light-use runtimes expected similar.

price.notes: BB regular $3,499.95, on sale $2,999.95. NBC news reports this 64GB SKU periodically gets ~30% discounts.

reviews.quote: Our review unit with 32 GB RAM can allocate up to 24 GB for the GPU, while other SKUs can allocate up to 48 or 96 GB VRAM.
The integrated graphics card Radeon 8060S is by far the fastest x86 iGPU and is neck-and-neck with the GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop (with a TGP range between 65-75 Watts) in games.

praises: 64GB unified memory lets the 8060S allocate up to 48GB VRAM — 30-70B local LLMs and big Stable Diffusion workflows fit entirely in GPU memory
16-core Zen 5 multicore rivals the Ryzen 9 7945HX and Apple M4 Pro in a 1.23 kg detachable tablet
Radeon 8060S plays AAA titles at RTX 4070-laptop speeds despite no discrete GPU — FSR helps where DLSS is absent
180Hz no-PWM IPS touch with accurate color (ΔE 1.5) plus USB4, HDMI 2.1, microSD and Wi-Fi 7 in a tablet
Cheapest way into 64GB of Strix Halo unified memory — undercuts Strix Halo mini PCs with the same RAM once on sale
complaints: RAM is still soldered — you pay $400 over the 32GB SKU at Best Buy for memory you can never change or resell
Battery under load is poor (~51 min max-brightness load on the reviewed SKU) and NBC notes 64GB SKUs draw even more peak power
Turbo-mode fan noise is loud and the stereo speakers are weak — NBC explicitly recommends headphones
Only the M.2-2230 SSD is reachable; the rest of the chassis is sealed, so repairability is minimal
No HDR, ~27-nit minimum brightness too bright for dark rooms, and the touchscreen layer adds slight grain on bright content

design_philosophy: ASUS's 'gaming tablet' bet: a detachable 13.4-inch tablet packing the flagship Strix Halo APU, no discrete GPU needed since the 8060S iGPU matches an RTX 4070 laptop part. The 64GB config is the power-user tier of the line — same chassis and screen as the reviewed 32GB SKU but with double the unified memory, aimed squarely at local-AI and heavy creative workloads.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the 32GB GZ302EA-RU073W config reviewed by Notebookcheck (86.8%), per SHARED-flow-z13.md. Deltas for 64GB unified memory: ai_ml +1.0 (VRAM allocation up to 48GB per NBC — larger LLMs/SD workflows fit), creative_work +0.5 (bigger projects in RAM/VRAM), productivity +0.5 (headroom for heavy multitasking). Gaming unchanged (same iGPU; extra VRAM doesn't raise raster at these budgets). NBC notes higher peak power draw on 64GB SKUs but light-use battery comparable, so battery held at 7.0. Pro-vs-user calibration from SHARED file applied (battery-under-load, fan noise, sealed chassis).
